newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index firms on Slovnaft gains.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index firms on Slovnaft gains.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, with gains to oil refinery Slovnaft pushing the SAX index up 1.46 points to 202.59.
Slovnaft closed up 36 crowns at 936, though on thin volume, offsetting losses to oil and gas storage firm Nafta, down 100 crowns to 1,800, and bank VUB down 15 crowns at 1,745.
But brokers said the bourse remains mired in a general downturn despite the rise in the index.
"Tuesday's gains to Slovnaft were made just by a single block deal, literally in the very last seconds of the session," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said.
"The closing price in Slovnaft was a bit overheated, as I think the issue deserves the price level at about 900 crowns," he added.
Analysts said the bourse is still plagued by low liquidity with the foreign investors likely waiting for a further decline in prices.
Overall volume decreased to 640,632 shares, from 1.034,245 shares traded on Monday, while turnover rose to 430.83 million crowns, from 377.61 million.
